newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's gasoline consumption up, leaded fuel down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's gasoline consumption up, leaded fuel down.

text.p: Mexico's gasoline demand is on the rise, but less leaded gasoline is being sold, state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said.
Total gasoline demand rose by three percent in the first half of 1997, to 492,000 barrels per day, Pemex said in a statement late on Thursday.
"Since the first half of last year, the national demand for gasolines reactivated, as a consequence of the economic recovery," Pemex said.
Leaded gasoline consumption slipped to 26 percent of total gasoline demand for the first half of 1997, from a high 42 percent in the first six months of 1996, Pemex said.
"In the first days of July, the sales of (leaded) Nova gasoline were 15 percent of the nation's total gasoline demand," Pemex said.

The oil monopoly said demand for leaded gasoline has fallen because of "consumer preference," but critics say Pemex has choked off the supply of Nova leaded gasoline, and allowed only a few gas stations to keep selling the fuel.
Leaded gasoline is not longer used in the states of Baja California, Chihuahua, Nuevo Leon and Tamaulipas, Pemex said.
